hero.headline: Two Martin County brush fires contained as Florida Forest Service warns of more to come this summer
hero.body:
Two brush fires broke out in Martin County this week, including one sparked by a lightning strike. Both fires are now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service, which says the conditions that fuel these fires are not going away anytime soon but residents should not be alarmed.

David Grubitch, a mitigation specialist and spokesperson with the Florida Forest Service, said this is their peak season for brush fires. The intense summertime heat is drying out fine dead fuels across the region. When lightning strikes occur, these dried fuels are receptive and ready to ignite. Grubitch explained that the combination of hot conditions and frequent lightning activity creates ongoing fire risk throughout the summer months. He said residents should expect these conditions to persist as long as the heat continues.

Grubitch noted that while rain often extinguishes these fires immediately, the situation is not always straightforward. Sometimes fires travel underground after a lightning strike and can resurface days later, even after rain has fallen. This means that a fire that appears to be out can unexpectedly flare up again, requiring continued monitoring from the Florida Forest Service. The department remains vigilant in tracking these fires to ensure they are truly extinguished and not simply smoldering beneath the surface.

The Florida Forest Service emphasized that the public plays a crucial role in helping the department respond quickly to brush fires. Grubitch stressed that residents should never assume someone else has already called in a brush fire when they spot one. If you see something, say something, he said, as it can make all the difference in how quickly crews are able to get a fire under control. The faster the department is notified about a fire, the more quickly they can deploy resources to contain it before it spreads. With peak fire season continuing throughout the summer, officials are counting on residents to remain alert and report any signs of smoke or fire immediately.

cards.headline: Jannik Sinner defends Wimbledon title with win over Alexander Zverev
cards.teaser: Top-ranked Jannik Sinner beat Alexander Zverev 6-7 (7), 7-6 (2), 6-3, 6-4 on Sunday for his second consecutive Wimbledon title and fifth Grand Slam championship.
cards.body:
Sinner's victory at the All England Club came in his first tournament since a second-round meltdown at the French Open. The Italian ripped a forehand winner up the line on his first match point and dropped to the grass on his back in celebration. It was Sinner's 10th straight victory over Zverev, who was coming off his first Grand Slam title at the French Open.

Zverev appeared bothered by a knee issue following a slip on the grass at a key point in the third set. Zverev slipped and appeared to hyper-extend his right knee as he attempted to change directions behind the baseline at 3-3 in the third set, 2 hours and 42 minutes into the match. Sinner helped his opponent up off the grass, but Zverev appeared slightly hampered and handed Sinner the first break of the match and a 5-3 lead in the third.

Prince William joined his wife Kate and two of their children for the final in a star-studded Royal Box that also included actors Dustin Hoffman, Nicole Kidman and Ben Stiller. Despite the defeat in the final, Zverev will leapfrog Carlos Alcaraz into the No. 2 spot in the rankings on Monday. Alcaraz missed both the French Open and Wimbledon this year due to a right wrist injury.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Three-Game Skid With 4-1 Win Over Jupiter
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed o
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed only minutes to take control. The first three batters of the game all reached and scored before an out was recorded. Elian Peña opened with a single, Mike Tauchman doubled him home, and Trey Snyder followed with a two-run homer off Walin Castillo for a 3-0 lead.

Julio Zayas added a solo shot with two outs in the third to push the margin to 4-0.

That was more than enough for starter Emilio Obispo, who threw five shutout innings and lowered his season ERA to 1.82. He scattered four singles, walked three and struck out six to earn his fourth win of the year.

Obispo worked out of trouble when it mattered. He struck out Josh Hogue to strand the bases loaded in the third, induced a double play to end the fourth, and retired the side in order in the fifth to finish his outing.

Jupiter loaded the bases against Calvin Ziegler in the sixth. Ziegler struck out Jake McCutheon for the second out before Zack Mack entered and ended the threat with a popout. Mack went 2.1 innings and allowed one unearned run, which came in the eighth when Andres Valor stole third and scored on a throwing error.

Elwis Mijares closed it out with a 1-2-3 ninth on 11 pitches for his second save.

Tauchman, rehabbing a torn meniscus, went 1 for 3 with the double, an RBI and a run while playing six innings in left field in his first rehab game with St. Lucie. Snyder led the offense at 2 for 4 with the homer and two RBI.

The Mets (5-13, 38-46) and Hammerheads (8-12, 45-41) close their six-game series Sunday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. A win would give St. Lucie its first 3-3 series split of 2026. First pitch is 12:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Linda Noskova wins Wimbledon after recovering from five blown match points
cards.teaser: Czech player Linda Noskova recovered from a second-set meltdown to beat Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final on Saturday for her first Grand Slam trophy.
cards.body:
Linda Noskova recovered from a second-set meltdown in which she wasted five match points to overcome Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final on Saturday for her first Grand Slam trophy. The 21-year-old became the third Czech woman in four years to win Wimbledon, after Marketa Vondrousova in 2023 and Barbora Krejcikova in 2024. Petra Kvitova, who won Wimbledon in 2011 and 2014, was in attendance for the final.

Martina Navratilova, who won a record nine singles titles at the All England Club, looked on from the Royal Box, where she was seated next to Kate, the Princess of Wales, who was due to present the Venus Rosewater Dish trophy to Noskova. Muchova and Noskova played doubles together at the 2024 Paris Olympics and finished fourth. In the men's final on Sunday, top-ranked Jannik Sinner will attempt to defend his title against French Open champion Alexander Zverev.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie ranked 67th most stressed city in the US, cited as 42nd most financially stressed
cards.teaser: A new WalletHub study ranked Port St. Lucie as the 67th most stressed city in the United States, with the report citing the city as the 42nd most financially stressed in America.
cards.body:
A new study released this month by WalletHub examined stress levels across American cities, finding that Port St. Lucie ranked 67th among the most stressed cities in the nation and 42nd for financial stress specifically. The study compared 182 cities using 39 different metrics, including average weekly work hours, unemployment rate, divorce and suicide rates.

Florida cities generally performed well in the rankings, with none appearing in the top 35 most stressed. Jacksonville topped the list for Florida at 37th nationally. In South Florida, Miami ranked 50th overall, with affordable housing cited as fourth worst in the United States. Fort Lauderdale came in at 83rd on the list.

WalletHub analyst Chip Lupo explained that while some stress stems from factors beyond individual control, such as issues with family, friends or employers, location plays a significant role in stress levels. Cities with high crime rates, weak economies, less effective public health and congested transportation systems naturally lead to elevated stress levels for residents, he said. Lupo noted that when moving, people should consider how a certain city may impact their mental health, not just their financial opportunities. The report found that money, health and the economy all remain top stressors for Americans.

The five most stressed cities in the United States were Detroit, Baltimore, Cleveland, Memphis and Shreveport, Louisiana. On the opposite end of the spectrum, Fremont, California, in the Bay Area, topped the list of least stressed cities. The notably affluent area has average home prices of about $1.5 million. Following Fremont were South Burlington, Vermont, and Bismarck and Fargo, both in North Dakota.

cards.headline: Karolina Muchova ends Coco Gauff's Wimbledon run in dramatic tiebreaker
cards.teaser: Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday to become the fourth Czech woman in six years to reach the final.
cards.body:
The ninth-ranked Muchova will face either Linda Noskova or Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine in Saturday's final. It will be Muchova's second Grand Slam final after losing to Iga Swiatek in the 2023 French Open championship match. Muchova is the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the Wimbledon final. The other Czech women in the Wimbledon final recently were Karolina Pliskova, runner-up in 2021, Marketa Vondrousova, champion in 2023, and Barbora Krejcikova, champion in 2024.

For the seventh-ranked American Gauff, it was still her most successful Wimbledon. Previously, Gauff had gone only as far as the fourth round three times, including during her breakthrough run as a 15-year-old in 2019. Muchova's 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker on Centre Court. The men's semifinals on Friday feature top-ranked and defending champion Jannik Sinner against seven-time Wimbledon winner Novak Djokovic and French Open champion Alexander Zverev against British wild card Arthur Fery.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie teen to serve as flag bearer at FIFA World Cup finals
cards.teaser: Enrique Rosario Liz, a Port St. Lucie teenager named Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, was surprised Friday at the Boys & Girls Club
cards.body:
Enrique Rosario Liz, a Port St. Lucie teenager named Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, was surprised Friday at the Boys & Girls Club of St. Lucie County in Fort Pierce with a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. He will serve as one of 12 club members from across the country selected to be an official Coca-Cola flag bearer at the FIFA World Cup finals on July 19. The surprise came courtesy of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America and their partnership with the Coca-Cola Company. When the box containing the news was walked into the room surrounded by fellow club members, his reaction was immediate. "I mean, this is so insane," Rosario Liz said. Along with the trip, he also received official gear inside the box.

Rosario Liz had already been juggling a packed summer, preparing for move-in at the University of Florida and an internship, but said the World Cup had been on his mind. "My time is really being taken up by the World Cup right now, forcing my parents to watch every game," Rosario Liz said. He credited the Boys & Girls Club with shaping who he has become as a leader. "The club really helped me to find what my leadership style was going to be, and really redefined what my definition of leadership was," Rosario Liz said. The recognition as a flag bearer comes after his selection as Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region, one of the highest honors given by the Boys & Girls Clubs of America.

As one of only 12 club members chosen nationally for this role, Rosario Liz will represent not only his local club in St. Lucie County but also youth organizations across the country at the World Cup finals. "The Boys & Girls Clubs has been my everything," he said. He closed with a message for younger members at the club. "Please stay with your Boys & Girls Clubs, because one day I want to see each and every one of you in the same position that I am in right now," Rosario Liz said.

The announcement marks a significant milestone for the Port St. Lucie teen as he prepares to transition to college life at the University of Florida while taking on this prestigious international role at the World Cup finals. The opportunity showcases the impact of the Boys & Girls Clubs program on young leaders and highlights the partnership between the youth organization and the Coca-Cola Company in providing exceptional experiences for outstanding club members.

hero.headline: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse offers 165 years of history with panoramic ocean views
hero.teaser: The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, built in 1860, offers a 105-step climb to panoramic views of the Atlantic Ocean, Jupiter Inlet, and Loxahatchee and Indian rivers.
hero.body:
The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse has stood watch over Florida's Atlantic coastline for more than 165 years since its construction in 1860. The red brick tower rises above the inlet, where it has guided countless ships navigating the waters along the coast. Today, visitors can experience the same journey that lighthouse keepers once made nightly as they climbed to maintain the beacon that warned mariners of the dangerous coastline.

The climb to the top requires ascending 105 steps via a narrow spiral staircase inside the tower. Lighthouse keepers historically made this trek night after night to keep the powerful Fresnel lens shining for ships at sea. The physical demands of the climb reflect the dedication required of those who once maintained this vital navigational aid. The narrow staircase adds to the authentic historical experience, giving modern visitors a glimpse into the working conditions of 19th and 20th century lighthouse keepers.

From the gallery at the top of the lighthouse, panoramic views reveal the Atlantic Ocean stretching eastward while the turquoise waters of the Jupiter Inlet flow below, meeting the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers. Boats glide through the channel as the sea breeze provides relief from Florida's warm weather. The vantage point offers visitors a commanding view of the waterways that made this lighthouse so essential for maritime navigation. The perspective from above shows why this location was chosen for the lighthouse and how keepers could monitor ship traffic and weather conditions.

The museum grounds feature restored historic buildings that preserve and share the story of the lighthouse's past. The site's history spans from its construction in the years before the Civil War through its operational years as an active Coast Guard station. These buildings provide context for understanding how the lighthouse functioned as more than just a tower with a light, but as a complete station where keepers and their families lived and worked. The grounds offer visitors a comprehensive look at lighthouse operations and the role this beacon played in coastal navigation and safety over more than a century and a half of service.
